evidence.excerpt:
Physics-based models connect scientific explanation with quantitative prediction.
Constructing them requires selecting physical processes, defining states and gov-
erning equations, specifying couplings, and identifying parameters from experi-
ments. Existing AI systems remain limited in making these model structure deci-
sions autonomously. We introduce EvoSim, a self-evolving AI scientist for physi-
cal modeling. It uses experimental discrepancies to drive mechanism and equation
revisions and held-out experimental data to test physical plausibility. Exploration
traces make updates to knowledge, skills, and multi-agent orchestration. This co-
evolution improves physics-based models and EvoSim's ability to select mecha-
nisms, diagnose failures, and coordinate research. We evaluate EvoSim on two
industrial battery modeling tasks. It predicts lithium-metal-plating onset from 25
to 45 °C

Model.EvoSim starts from a one-dimensional porous-electrode model for electrolyte transport,
electronic conduction, particle diffusion, and graphite intercalation. It adds a parallel plating
and stripping reaction driven by the local plating overpotential. Onset is defined by a capacity-
normalized accumulated irreversible-lithium threshold. The 14 training conditions identify a shared
plating exchange-current scale and a bounded rate-dependent fraction that converts accumulated de-
position into irreversible lithium. The model is then fixed before prediction of the six validation
conditions.

The dynamic-voltage case evaluates one fixed model structure by leave-one-temperature cross-
validation on complete driving traces. The evaluation contains eight temperature folds and 16 traces.
In each fold, both the DST and US06 traces at the held-out temperature are excluded from parameter
identification, and both are evaluated after the fold-specific parameters are identified. We report two
pre-defined individual-condition results in the main text. Section C.4 gives the split definition and
the reported held-out results.
These checks answer different scientific questions. Agreement with the development measurements
tests whether the constructed equations and calibrated parameters describe the observed cell. So-
lution and physical checks test whether the implemented model solves the stated equations and
respects their constraints. Cross-validation

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline model-accuracy claims are established on held-out validation conditions and leave-one-temperature folds excluded from parameter identification, while the Scientific Evolution effect is measured on fixed procedures in separate paired runs.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Held-out experimental measurements for plating onset and dynamic voltage, plus fixed-procedure paired runs with manual failure labeling for the Scientific Evolution comparison.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Training-condition residuals and solver/implementation checks used to select model structures, parameters, and retained procedures.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics (1.79% MAE on plating onset, 7.62 mV RMSE on dynamic voltage) and significant failure reductions (36.4% relative drop in model/physics failures) are supported by detailed tables, code update logs, and held-out empirical evaluations.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is conducted on two distinct physical battery tasks (lithium-plating onset under fast charging and dynamic terminal voltage under driving cycles) with strict train/validation splits and leave-one-temperature cross-validation, corroborated by statistical analysis (McNemar test) across 45 paired modeling tasks.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance claims are validated on separate, held-out experimental operating conditions and cross-validation folds that were completely excluded during parameter identification and procedural optimization.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Evaluation on strictly held-out physical datasets (held-out validation temperatures and charging conditions for plating onset and dynamic voltage) using objective physical error metrics (RMSE/MAE in mV and SOC percentage points).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Discrepancy signals between candidate model solver outputs and training experimental datasets, combined with automated implementation and solution verification checks within the modeling loop.

primary.limitations: The transfer of dynamic voltage prediction is validated across unseen temperatures within known driving cycle profiles rather than completely unseen duty cycles, and certain complex failure modes remain unresolved across challenging physical tasks.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology couples LLM-driven hypothesis generation with rigorous implementation, numerical solver execution in COMSOL Multiphysics, and structured validation against experimental observations. The scientific evolution loop explicitly distinguishes between model candidate acceptance and the extraction of vetted, conditional procedural knowledge.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a thorough, well-controlled experimental framework featuring multi-task evaluations, rigorous isolation, and clear ablation comparisons between baseline, naive memory, and scientific evolution. Claims are appropriately scoped and corroborated by empirical measurements.
primary.scoped_contribution: EvoSim is an AI framework that autonomously formulates, implements, and refines physics-based battery models via multi-agent hypothesis generation and solver-in-the-loop numerical validation, while accumulating procedural modeling strategies across tasks.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a thorough, well-controlled experimental framework featuring multi-task evaluations, rigorous isolation, and clear ablation comparisons between baseline, naive memory, and scientific evolution. Claims are appropriately scoped and corroborated by empirical measurements.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The transfer of dynamic voltage prediction is validated across unseen temperatures within known driving cycle profiles rather than completely unseen duty cycles, and certain complex failure modes remain unresolved across challenging physical tasks.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to autonomous/deep research workflows based on screening evidence.
